PRIVILEGED - WORK PRODUCT
TO: Monica Tran-Nguyen | FROM: Kevin Brashear | DATE: November 8, 2024
RE: Unified Litigation Hold - Kovach Matter and SEC Informal Inquiry: Custodians, Data Sources, Spoliation Exposure, Coordination

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Issue one consolidated hold today, tagged K (Kovach), S (SEC) or both. (b) Within 24 hours stop the Teams 90-day purge, Salesforce 18-month batch job, backup rotation and NXF-FS01 migration. (c) Chat loss for roughly May-August 2024 is real and overlaps windows Stadler Raines singled out. (d) Several file facts change the Nov 4-7 email assumptions (Section 6).

2. TRIGGER DATE AND EXPOSURE
Law. Duty arises when a party has notice evidence is relevant to litigation or should have known. Guzman v. Jones, 804 F.3d 707 (5th Cir. 2015) (binding in federal court in Texas; adverse inference requires bad faith). For ESI, FRCP 37(e) governs: sanctions require that ESI that should have been preserved was lost because of a failure to take reasonable steps and cannot be restored or replaced; measures no greater than necessary to cure prejudice (37(e)(1)); adverse inference or default only on a finding of intent to deprive (37(e)(2)). A state-court Sabine Pilot claim would apply Brookshire Bros. v. Aldridge, 438 S.W.3d 9 (Tex. 2014) (duty plus intentional or negligent breach; negligent spoliation supports an instruction only if the other side is irreparably deprived of any meaningful ability to present a claim or defense). Separately, 18 U.S.C. 1519 criminalizes knowing destruction with intent to impede a matter within federal agency jurisdiction "in relation to or in contemplation of" it; no pending proceeding is required. Routine purges that continue after the October 28 SEC letter, with knowledge, are the risk point.

Triggers (Policy 4.1 itself lists whistleblower complaints, internal investigations, demand letters and SEC inquiries):
- Jul 15: PIP signed "under protest" (plaintiff may argue).
- Aug 5: written complaint to Audit Chair (Stadler's date). Aug 20: Audit Committee investigation opens.
- Aug 29: Kovach told Pinnacle the PIP was retaliatory (documented to Company counsel). I regard Aug 29 as the strongest realistic date; Aug 5 is a credible plaintiff argument.
- Sep 12: termination; Company handed him a release expressly covering SOX/whistleblower claims, which evidences anticipation. Floor for us: Sep 12.
- Oct 3: demand letter with express Teams preservation demand (indefensible to argue later). Oct 18: Pinnacle advises suspending retention. Oct 28: SEC written preservation notice.
Recommend we internally assume Aug 29 and not argue later than Sep 12.

Teams chat loss (90-day purge; as of Nov 8 the cutoff is about Aug 10, advancing daily; your Nov 6 figure of Aug 8 has moved). Chat created before the cutoff, but after (trigger minus 90 days), was lost during the delay:
- Aug 5 trigger: May 7 - Aug 10 lost. Aug 29: May 31 - Aug 10. Sep 12: Jun 14 - Aug 10 (Jun 14 is Kovach's first complaint). Oct 3: Jul 5 - Aug 10. Oct 28: Jul 30 - Aug 10.
- Even on the Oct 3 date, Jul 5-15 (inside Stadler's Jul 2-15 Sokolova/Ellicott/Purdy window, expressly demanded) was lost after written notice, and 36 days passed (Oct 3 - Nov 8) with no action. That is the hardest fact for us. Mitigant: the pre-existing (Feb 2023), tenant-wide setting supports absence of intent (37(e)(2)); negligence exposure under 37(e)(1) and Brookshire remains. Policy 3.1 is silent on chat, and IT says the 90-day rule was set "with the prior General Counsel's office" in Feb 2023, yet the policy was revised Feb 15, 2023 over your approval.
- Possible recovery: Microsoft documents that expired chats sit in SubstrateHolds for at least 1 day and are purged in the next timer-job cycle (typically 1-7 days). Place holds today; the latest purged days may be rescued. Export the M365 audit log now (metadata only).
- Replaceability (37(e) factor): the same conversations may survive in email, Kovach's retained mailbox, Salesforce, SAP, the S: drive, texts, Kovach's phone (likely limited; Teams mobile caches are thin and sign-out probably cleared them), and witness testimony.

Other post-trigger losses to quantify (not yet assumed): (i) Salesforce records marked Inactive Feb 5 - May 8, 2023 were auto-deleted Aug 5 - Nov 8, 2024; those deleted in the last 15 days (inactive roughly Apr 24 - May 8, 2023) may still be in the recycle bin and should be restored today. (ii) Kovach's OneDrive and laptop (Section 4). (iii) Pre-April 2024 Veritas gaps (421 mailboxes) and the May 15, 2024 Exchange decommissioning predate any trigger, so they are a collection problem rather than spoliation, but document it before it is characterized otherwise. Cross-reference the remediation log against the custodian list today.
Disclosure of the Teams purge to the SEC staff (cooperation credit) and Stadler Raines is a separate strategic decision for you and outside counsel; keep this assessment privileged. SEC request 4 covers chats and the Nov 27 response date forces the issue.

3. CUSTODIANS
Tier 1 (hold, collect first):
- Sokolova (CFO) K+S: Jun 14/Jul 2 complaints; PIP reports; rev-rec; auditor.
- Ellicott (CEO) K+S: supervisor, approved PIP, terminated Kovach.
- Purdy (VP HR) K: PIP, termination, severance, paper file; an accused actor, so no self-collection; Ridgeway takes custody of originals.
- Herrera (interim VP) K+S: Salesforce, PIP CRM audits, directives, Kovach's forwarded mail; controls the "Inactive" flag, so freeze it.
- Chen (Controller) K+S: Jun 28; rev-rec entries; return reserve.
- Ainsley (Audit Chair) K+S: see Section 5.
- Kovach (former) K+S: all Company-held data (mailbox, Teams, OneDrive, S: drive, Salesforce user data, SuccessFactors, expense/card records, laptop) plus a third-party preservation demand for personal data.
Tier 2 (interviewees; all should be custodians, answering your question): Collings, Muñoz, Patwardhan (Collings used emails and texts with distributors; Patwardhan holds directive emails; K+S), Jessup (VP Ops; "ship-ahead" shipments, WMS/shipping records; S primarily). Extend notices to the other 11 regional managers and 2 sales ops staff; collect in phases.
Tier 3 additions: Controller's revenue accounting, AR/returns (RMA) and credit staff (S); Houston/Dallas logistics managers (S); internal audit, IR, Corporate Secretary (S); executive assistants; other Audit Committee members; HR staff (K); IT (Novotny, Halverson, Dasgupta); Legal (you and me). Third parties: Pinnacle, Caldwell Thornton.
Unique to Kovach: Purdy, HR staff, payroll data. Unique to SEC: Jessup, logistics, accounting/AR/returns, internal audit, IR, Corporate Secretary. Others: both.
Relevant period: Jan 1, 2023 for sales, returns and finance data (year-over-year comparisons), Jan 1, 2024 for general communications, Kovach's entire tenure for performance records, running through resolution (include Q4 2024 returns). Track K and S separately in the hold log (different release criteria).

4. DATA SOURCES AND IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
1. M365 mail and Teams: eDiscovery holds today on all Tier 1-3 mailboxes, including Kovach's shared mailbox. Group chats live in each member's mailbox; channel messages live in group mailboxes, so hold the Sales, Finance, Executive and Operations team mailboxes (channel chat purges at 1 year, so Jan 2024 channel content begins expiring in January 2025). Suspend the 90-day chat deletion tenant-wide; propagation can take days, so use individual holds meanwhile.
2. Veritas Enterprise Vault NXF-EV01: hold and forensic image by Ridgeway; Jan-Mar 2024 email sits here (SEC period).
3. Salesforce: suspend the nightly batch now; restore recycle-bin items; full export (Data Loader) of accounts, opportunities, activities, field history and setup audit trail for channel accounts. Field history ages out of the UI at 18 months, so export now (verify against our configuration). The batch job also deletes distributor contracts that Policy 3.3 requires kept 7 years.
4. NXF-FS01: forensic image (8-10 hours) before further migration; 40% of Sales files are "stale" and slated for deletion. Policy 3.6 requires 60 days' notice to Legal before decommissioning (due by December 2) and Legal's written sign-off before destruction. IT's end-of-extended-support rationale is off: Windows Server 2016 support runs to January 2027; the drivers are the hardware contract and lease.
5. Backups: Policy 3.6 rotates backups at 90 days; pull and retain the oldest sets now (about Aug 10 forward).
6. SAP: low risk; take targeted extracts (2-3 days) with change logs.
7. Kovach's returned Dell laptop: absent from IT's inventory. Locate, sequester and image it today; if already reimaged, document when and why.
8. Kovach's OneDrive and SharePoint/OneDrive of all custodians: absent from IT's inventory; check Kovach's OneDrive deletion status immediately (default post-departure retention is often 30 days, so it may already be in a recycle stage).
9. Not yet inventoried: SuccessFactors, PIP drafts/metadata, WMS/shipping systems (Houston, Dallas), expense/card data, voicemail, calendars, board portal.
10. Mobile and text messages: about 45 VP-level-and-above BYOD users lack MDM, and regional managers (not BYOD-eligible) apparently used texts with distributors. Interview custodians on texts and messaging apps; notice should require disabling auto-delete.
11. Paper: Secure the HR personnel file and 8th-floor Sales cabinets (channel agreements, notes); label per Policy 5.
12. Monterrey (file server, separate Salesforce org): preserve for now; the demand letter says Kovach's territories included Canada, Mexico and Latin America, HR says U.S. only.

5. AINSLEY AND PRIVILEGE
Preservation is not production: Ainsley goes on hold now, and nothing is segregated away from preservation. The two-track protocol is for review. Key points:
- Investigation privilege belongs to the Audit Committee/Company; the Committee should approve the protocol.
- Pinnacle should not collect Ainsley's data. It conducted the investigation, will be a custodian of its own file, and now defends the Company; collection by the firm whose work product is at issue invites attack. Use Ridgeway under a counsel-directed engagement (confirm the Nov 1 Ridgeway engagement runs through counsel to protect work product), with Pinnacle conducting privilege review.
- Ask where Ainsley communicates (personal email, texts, board portal) and hold all.
- Fiduciary exception: Garner v. Wolfinbarger, 430 F.2d 1093 (5th Cir. 1970), and Wal-Mart Stores v. Indiana Elec. Workers Pension Tr. Fund IBEW, 95 A.3d 1264 (Del. 2014) (Nexfield is a Delaware corporation) apply to stockholder suits for good cause. Kovach, a non-stockholder SOX complainant, and the SEC are not within that doctrine as stated; the greater risk is waiver by producing the investigation to the SEC or relying on it as a defense. Seek a Fed. R. Evid. 502(d) order if suit is filed.

6. ISSUES IN THE FILE THAT CHANGE THE EMAIL ASSUMPTIONS
- Kovach's Company data is intact and in our control (mailbox post-April 1); only personal-device data is not.
- BYOD acknowledgment (Jan 8, 2021) has Kovach consenting to inspection and agreeing to "cooperate with data preservation and collection requirements as directed by the Legal Department." Cite it in the letter. IT dates enrollment Apr 3, 2020, but BYOD is VP-and-above and he became VP Jan 1, 2021; reconcile the dates.
- Preservation letter: send this week to Stadler Raines only (Texas Rule 4.02), covering the iPhone (Outlook, Teams, Salesforce apps), iCloud backups, personal email/messaging and any Company documents retained; propose neutral imaging; add a carve-out preserving his communications with the SEC (Exchange Act Rule 21F-17).
- Pinnacle's October 18 engagement covers only Kovach defense, excluding regulatory matters, and is unsigned. No counsel is engaged for the SEC inquiry (response due Nov 27). Resolve now; consider independent SEC counsel.
- Pinnacle served the Audit Committee and now defends the Company under the same partner; Stadler Raines and Pinnacle list the identical street address and suite (1700 Louisiana, Suite 3400). Confirm whether this is a document error or an affiliation and obtain the conflicts-check detail.
- You approved the retention policy and I drafted the trigger analysis; have outside counsel review the timeline independently.

7. COORDINATION AND NEXT STEPS
Today: IT written confirmations (Policy 4.2(4)) of the suspensions; eDiscovery holds; Salesforce, Teams, backup and FS01 freezes; laptop and OneDrive status. Within 48 hours: hold notice (48-hour acknowledgment, Policy 4.3), custodian interviews, remediation-log cross-reference, Vault and FS01 images, paper custody. Within one week: Stadler Raines letter, Audit Committee protocol, SEC counsel decision; quarterly reminders; hold log. Share this memo with Ms. Drummond Monday, as directed, limited to counsel.
